claims.statement: Synchronization separates configuration ZIP upload, environment profile replacement and receiver testdata POSTs: profiles and testdata are not included in get_zip_config, and download retrieves environment/configuration rather than receiver testdata.
Upload, download and status select <profile>-env.json relative to their working directory; the default profile is test and profile names may include a directory path.

The CLI detects connector mode using manifest.json under connector_dir; regular upload directly invokes upload(), whereas connector upload expands and locally validates, uploads from the expanded directory, then authenticates unless skip-auth is set.

SesamCmdClient.test calls upload, waits again for deployment, runs the requested iterations and verifies; the test dispatcher does not itself execute the connector-upload expansion/validation/authentication branch.
The CLI normally gates online operations on developer_mode; force allows upload and download on non-developer subscriptions, and upload forwards force through SesamNode.put_config to upload_config.

get_zip_config overwrites an existing sesam-config.zip with a deflated archive of recursively discovered pipes/systems .conf.json files and optional root node metadata, retaining directory paths rather than flattening filenames.

zip_dir filters pipe/system configuration using exact normalized forward-slash paths whenever whitelisted_files is not None, while root node metadata uses a separate existing-file and falsy-list-or-explicit-membership check.

Regular-config ZIP construction performs regex replacement of {{@ variable @}} placeholders using .jinja_vars without modifying local pipe/system files; connector files and root node metadata are written directly without this substitution path.

get_zip_config normally removes the temporary disk ZIP after reading bytes; dump retains it, and upload -dump retains the initial local archive before subsequent in-memory metadata changes, so it need not equal the submitted archive.

Download -dump saves the remote ZIP after metadata normalization and formatting but still performs local deletion/extraction; status -dump first builds/removes the local ZIP then saves remote ZIP bytes after metadata normalization without formatting all members.

Upload computes node metadata in memory with disable_user_pipes True by default or False with enable-user-pipes, eager_load_microservices False by default or True with enable-eager-ms, and enable_cpp_extensions False only when disable-cpp-extensions is specified.

replace_file_in_zipfile replaces existing matching members only and never inserts an absent member; upload's computed metadata changes are therefore absent from the submitted ZIP if node metadata was missing or excluded during ZIP construction.

Download and status normalize remote node metadata against the current local metadata: only remote disable_user_pipes True, enable_cpp_extensions False and eager_load_microservices False are restored to local values or removed if no local key exists; absent remote metadata is left unchanged, and opposite values are not normalized.

remove_task_manager_settings can raise KeyError when removal of a sole enable_cpp_extensions False key deletes global_defaults, because its subsequent eager_load_microservices condition indexes the deleted section.
upload reads the selected profile using utf-8-sig and rethrows missing/invalid-profile errors before the method's optional sink deletion or environment replacement.

With upload-delete-sink-datasets, upload calls delete_all_sink_datasets before environment/configuration upload and rethrows deletion failures; this cleanup is not whitelist-scoped or a full reset, and flag help warns that prior data/config may still influence tests.

Upload overlays ../.additional_parameters.json onto the selected profile with warnings for overwritten keys, submits the resulting replacement object through put_env_vars without fetching/merging the remote environment, and only then builds and submits the configuration ZIP.

Offline validate expands the connector and checks template sink constraints plus expanded JSON/connector conventions; only connector upload dispatch invokes that local validator, while regular upload relies on the separate backend configuration upload/validation boundary.

Backend config-upload exceptions with parsed_response become UploadException using validation_errors; other exceptions are rethrown, and UploadException is logged with exit status 1 by the dispatcher.

UploadException reports posted-config._id and uses ordered verbosity branches: verbose shows error-level config-errors, extra_verbose shows all config-errors, and extra_extra_verbose shows the whole validation record; without flags its report can contain only framing headers.

Upload is ordered remote mutation rather than transactional orchestration: sink deletion and environment replacement may succeed before ZIP/backend validation fails, and configuration acceptance may precede deployment/testdata failure, with no compensating rollback code.

Deployment waiting checks user pipes in runtime Deploying state, excluding listed non-user origins and :singlenode pipes, polls one pipe using zero-timeout checks with five-second loop sleeps, and raises RuntimeError after a still-failing check exceeds the default 30-minute timeout; receiver uploads start only after this wait returns.

Testdata discovery recursively accepts case-insensitive .json suffixes and maps each filename's basename without extension to a case-preserving pipe ID, filtering only when whitelisted_pipes is nonempty; nested duplicate basenames can target the same receiver without deterministic parallel ordering.

upload_testdata parses UTF-8 JSON with float by default or Decimal under do-float-as-decimal, sends the loaded payload as JSON, and treats JSON null as a successful no-POST return that callers count as uploaded; parsing occurs outside the receiver retry loop.

The receiver wrapper checks that the mapped pipe exists, resolves its receiver endpoint, POSTs the provided payload and returns response JSON; it does not locally classify the target as an input pipe.
Default testdata upload uses eight workers capped to job count and at least one; CLI parsing rejects counts below one and negative upload rates, while single-thread-upload ignores upload-workers.

Parallel testdata upload submits all jobs, collects all completed futures and logs a summary before raising an aggregate TestDataUploadException containing failed paths, pipe IDs and error strings, so successful partial uploads can coexist with command failure.
Sequential testdata upload fails fast on the first final error, does not process later jobs, and still logs per-job progress and a summary through finally blocks rather than aggregating failures.

Testdata progress is logged every 25 processed jobs and on the final job, summaries report totals and elapsed time, and missing/empty eligible testdata produces a no-data log; the parallel-success waiting-five-seconds message has no corresponding sleep.

The outer testdata retry loop allows four attempts total and retries response status 429 or any status at least 500, rejects other 4xx responses, and without a response retries only RequestException; delays use one-second-base exponential backoff plus uniform zero-to-one-second jitter.

A positive upload-rate uses a shared lock and monotonic next-slot timestamp to space outer testdata attempts by at least 1/rate seconds, sleeping outside the lock; zero is unlimited and the gate does not limit each POST in the receiver's inner retry loop.

The receiver has a separate 503-only retry loop with one-second sleeps until more than 60 seconds has elapsed, then raises for status; an exhausted 503 can trigger the outer retry loop again, and repeated POSTs are not guarded by an idempotency mechanism in this code.

Download creates/enters the expanded directory in connector mode, overwrites the selected profile with formatted remote environment using utf-8-sig before fetching configuration, then retrieves remote ZIP bytes via get_config_as_zip and applies metadata normalization.

Download deletes only top-level pipes/*.conf.json and systems/*.conf.json, protecting nonmatching paths when the whitelist file list is truthy; nested stale files and root node metadata are not removed by this deletion stage.

Download reformats every ZIP member as JSON then extracts the entire archive without a whitelist filter, so deletion-protected local files can still be overwritten and non-JSON members can fail formatting after deletions; failed download does not restore the previous profile or deleted files.

Regular-config download reverses .jinja_vars values into placeholders using regex substitution only in top-level pipes/systems .json files when both directories exist; it does not cover node metadata or nested files and nonunique/regex-sensitive values can cause unintended replacements.

Connector download invokes collapse_connector after extraction, reconstructing templates and rewriting manifest.json with best-effort textual parameter replacement, so it can overwrite connector source files in addition to expanded configuration.
Synchronization's direct format_json calls use the default style, which provides two-space indentation, conventional key ordering, Unicode output and a trailing newline.

Status uses get_zip_config for local membership and normalizes remote metadata; connector status compares an existing expanded directory without re-expansion and only logs an error when that directory is absent.

Status treats remote-only/local-only archive members as drift without whitelist filtering of the remote list, and compares local raw ZIP text to formatted remote JSON, making equivalent JSON with different local formatting reportable as drift.
Status formats both local profile JSON and remote environment before comparison; missing local profile logs an error but does not itself set the drift flag.

Status generates Python difflib.unified_diff text and diff controls its logging rather than detection; the external-diff requirement in help is stale, and status drift is logged rather than raised as a command failure.

Whitelisting is not a uniform operation scope: it does not constrain environment replacement, all-sink deletion, deployment waiting, remote extraction or status remote membership; a systems-only whitelist yields an empty pipe list and therefore does not restrict receiver jobs.
The -single option is parsed and advertised as a single-pipe option but is not consumed as an implemented scope restriction; it is distinct from the implemented single-thread-upload switch.

The fair-weather fixture deliberately excludes foo.conf.json from its whitelist and exercises test, update, status and download -dump after reset; its explicit download assertion checks archive existence rather than status drift text.

Conversion rewrites the selected conditional embedded source to http_endpoint and writes testdata named by the pipe's _id, including case preservation; the embedded-conversion fixture exercises conversion plus upload/run/verify and uses external diff -r to compare expected and generated directories.

Synchronization diagnostics can expose sensitive values through profile diffs, full validation records, .jinja_vars logging, connection failure token logging and receiver response logging, so shared examples and logs require redaction.
